scenes.narration: Scientists made students wear the most embarrassing T-shirt they could find. Then they counted who noticed.
scenes.art: a nervous college student wearing a cringe t-shirt printed with a cheesy smiling 1970s singer face, sweating, walking into a classroom door

scenes.narration: The shirt had a giant face of singer Barry Manilow on it. Students had rated it seriously embarrassing to wear.
scenes.art: a close up of a hilariously cheesy t-shirt print of a generic smiling 1970s crooner with big hair and sparkles, comedic

scenes.narration: The wearer walked into a room full of other students, sat down for a moment, and left.
scenes.art: a classroom full of students busy with their own work while one student in a silly t-shirt sits awkwardly in the corner

scenes.narration: Then the researchers asked: how many people noticed your shirt? The wearers guessed about half the room.
scenes.art: a worried student imagining a crowd of giant staring eyes pointing at their t-shirt, thought bubble

scenes.narration: The real number? Only about one in four.
scenes.art: the same classroom where almost nobody is looking up, one bored student barely glancing, comedic contrast

scenes.narration: Psychologists call this the spotlight effect. You feel like you're on stage, under a giant spotlight.
scenes.art: a young adult standing alone under a huge bright stage spotlight in a dark room, looking embarrassed

scenes.narration: But everyone else is standing under their own spotlight, worrying about themselves.
scenes.art: many young adults each standing under their own small spotlight, all looking worried about themselves and ignoring each other, funny

scenes.narration: It wasn't just about cringe, either. In another version, students wore a shirt they thought was cool. They still overestimated who noticed.
scenes.art: a confident student in sunglasses wearing a cool t-shirt striking a pose while nobody in the room looks

scenes.narration: So that awkward thing you said yesterday? Most people have probably already forgotten it.
scenes.art: a young adult lying awake in bed cringing at a memory replaying in a thought bubble, while friends sleep peacefully

scenes.narration: They were too busy worrying about their own awkward thing.
scenes.art: a row of people each with a tiny embarrassing memory cloud above their own head, all cringing, comedic

scenes.narration: So go ahead. Wear the shirt. What's the thing you think everyone still remembers?

post.title: Scientists made students wear the most embarrassing shirt 😳
post.description:
The spotlight effect: we think everyone notices us way more than they actually do. Proven with a Barry Manilow T-shirt.

Source: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky (2000) Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
